alex.ramos: Heads-up — noticed a p95 regression in canary after the kernel swap (v2.3.1). Route `ecomm-high` p95 jumped ~95ms -> ~235ms, kv_hit_ratio went 0.74 -> 0.52. Logs show bigger microbatches forming than usual.

samir.patel: saw alerts too. looks correlated with the kernel switch to the new prefetched-attn path — it increases per-token cost for short sequences unless batching stays small.

priya.chen: do we have the current continuous-batcher config for that route? token budget targets can blow up batch size and evict KV cache.

alex.ramos: pasting the canary route config we rolled: ```
route_rules:
  ecomm-high:
    token_budget_target: 1024
    max_batch_size: 256
    prefetch_window_ms: 20
    queue_policy: oldest_first_weight: 0.6
```

jordan.lee: woah 1024 token budget for ecomm-high seems high — traffic is mostly short seq (<= 64). the continuous batcher is waiting to hit token budget which causes large microbatches of many short requests; that explains kv churn and higher tail.

lee.morgan: KV hit ratio drop also suggests eviction pressure. big microbatches mean we stream through many different KV prefixes before reuse. check shard alignment and `kv_evicts` counters.

samir.patel: quick experiment suggestion: lower token_budget_target -> 400, reduce prefetch_window_ms -> 8, and bias queue_policy toward shorter sequences (weight small_seq higher). try as canary patch and watch p95 and kv_hit.

alex.ramos: will push canary patch with these values in ~30m. patch plan: 1) update route config for ecomm-high 2) enable extra perf counters (batch_formation_size, kv_evicts) 3) add alert: p95 > 160ms for 3m -> rollback.

infra-bot: deploybot: Starting canary config rollout for routes: ecomm-high (cluster A) — change_id=cbr-4801.

priya.chen: also add a short-term kernel fallback per-route if the p95 stays high. we should be able to route ecomm-high to kernel v2.2.x while the new kernels get tuned.

jordan.lee: long term: we should adapt token_budget_target automatically from observed seq length distribution and p95 SLOs (feedback loop). for now manual tweak.

samir.patel: can you run a quick `perf record` on a representative canary host to confirm hotspots? command I use: ```sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 60 && perf script | ./FlameGraph/stackcollapse-perf.pl | ./FlameGraph/flamegraph.pl > /tmp/canary.svg```

alex.ramos: running perf now, will upload flamegraph. also enabling `batch_formation_size` histogram in telemetry.

lee.morgan: FYI add metric: `batch.tokens_per_microbatch` and `route.kv_reuse_ratio` — make dashboards for ecomm-high and compare to baseline.

alex.ramos: patch pushed — token_budget_target=400, prefetch_window_ms=8, queue_policy updated. monitoring p95, kv_hit, batch_size. will report back in ~10m.

priya.chen: :thumbsup: if p95 drops to near baseline we can iterate a higher token target slowly with SLO-aware gating. otherwise rollback.

alex.ramos: quick update: 5m in — p95 down to ~120ms, kv_hit_ratio up to 0.68, avg microbatch size reduced from ~48 -> ~12. flamegraph points to ~35% time in attention kernel on short-seq path. sharing svg in thread.

samir.patel: nice! suggests batching heuristics were the main culprit not kernel correctness. follow-up: add automatic per-route token_target based on 95th-percentile seq_len * concurrency factor.

jordan.lee: agreed. file a short RFC for adaptive token targets + guardrails for kernel switches. i can draft.

alex.ramos: thanks all. if we hold for 15m and metrics stay stable i'll promote change to prod and schedule a postmortem doc with profiling artifacts. tagging @priya.chen and @samir.patel for next steps.

infra-bot: deploybot: Canary rollout cbr-4801 completed on cluster A (stable).

alex.ramos: closing loop — created RFC: /docs/rfcs/adaptive-token-budgeting (draft). will attach flamegraphs & metric diffs.
